query: Wind in a Jar On the dead-letter shelf, behind a parcel addressed to nobody, is a stoppered jar with a wind in it, going round and round. The label says FOR WHOEVER IS FAST ENOUGH. The loft master says someone flew with it once, before her time. Take the jar down The jar hums in your hands, and every broom in the loft leans toward you. The loft master writes your name on the jar's label, under a name too faded to read. Leave it on the shelf You leave it for whoever is fast enough. You fly your round. The jar's wind stirs the dead letters as you go.

The Fisherman Waves
The old fisherman in the reed beds has never waved at a courier. Today, seeing the jar strapped to your broom, he waves, and beckons you down. "That jar," he says. "I flew it once. Fastest year of my life."
